<solution>CD36 encodes the heavier protein.

- **ACOT7** (UniProt O00154, cytosolic acyl-CoA thioester hydrolase, 380 aa): **41.80 kDa** (average), 41.77 kDa monoisotopic
- **CD36** (UniProt P16671, platelet glycoprotein 4, 472 aa): **53.05 kDa** (average), 53.02 kDa monoisotopic

CD36 is ~11.3 kDa heavier.

Notes on the data: these are masses of the unmodified polypeptide chains (no signal-peptide cleavage or PTMs). CD36 is a heavily N-glycosylated membrane protein, so its mature form migrates at ~88 kDa on gels — the value here is the nascent chain only. Also, the UniProt JSON metadata for P16671 returned a truncated length field (354 aa) with an inconsistent molWeight, while the actual sequence in the same record and the FASTA endpoint give 472 aa; I used the sequence-derived value, which agrees with the canonical 53 kDa CD36.
